claims.claim: **Vulvovaginitis is common and usually resolves with simple measures.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval and vaginal conditions' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_and_vaginal_conditions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider pinworms** when a prepubertal child has distressing vaginal or perineal itch and/or pain at night.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval and vaginal conditions' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_and_vaginal_conditions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Recurrent UTI symptoms with negative cultures: assess for vulvodynia.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval and vaginal conditions' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_and_vaginal_conditions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Newborns** commonly have breast buds, white mucoid discharge, small vaginal blood loss and hymenal tags from maternal oestrogen; **bleeding in the first week of life needs no investigation or treatment.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval and vaginal conditions' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_and_vaginal_conditions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Abnormal vaginal bleeding:** foreign body, excoriation (vulvovaginitis, lichen sclerosus, pinworms), trauma including straddle injury or **sexual abuse**, **precocious puberty** (secondary sexual characteristics under 8 years), urethral prolapse, rarely tumour.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval and vaginal conditions' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_and_vaginal_conditions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider whether a perineal examination is needed** and discuss with a senior clinician. **Examine once, by the most suitable clinician**, with a senior clinician supervising/chaperoning alongside the parent, after explanation and consent.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval and vaginal conditions' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_and_vaginal_conditions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Position:** supine or semi-supine on a parent's lap in frog-leg, or lying on the side with knees to chest.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval and vaginal conditions' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_and_vaginal_conditions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mild vulval erythema is normal before puberty.** Pale atrophic patches suggest lichen sclerosus; pain on cotton-bud touch approaching the peri-hymenal area suggests vulvodynia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval and vaginal conditions' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_and_vaginal_conditions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Document by describing, not interpreting**, findings. ⚠️ **Offensive discharge with bleeding before menarche suggests a vaginal foreign body.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval and vaginal conditions' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_and_vaginal_conditions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Unclear cause or suspected vaginal foreign body: discuss with a gynaecologist.** Consider urine MCS.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval and vaginal conditions' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_and_vaginal_conditions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Profuse or offensive discharge: swab for MCS at the introitus only** — no internal vaginal swabs.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval and vaginal conditions' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_and_vaginal_conditions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Features:** vulval discomfort, itch, dysuria, discharge, redness. **Causes:** thin, alkaline prepubertal mucosa; moisture, poor hygiene, irritants; pinworms, bacterial overgrowth, STI, foreign body. **Most need no investigations.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval and vaginal conditions' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_and_vaginal_conditions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat:** explanation and reassurance, remove environmental causes, good hygiene and vulval care, **vinegar baths (½ cup white vinegar in a shallow bath)**; low-dose steroid cream for severe itch or excoriation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval and vaginal conditions' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_and_vaginal_conditions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pinworms: mebendazole 50 mg (over 6 months and 10 kg or less) or 100 mg (over 10 kg) orally as a single dose, repeated after 2 weeks**, and treat all household contacts.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval and vaginal conditions' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_and_vaginal_conditions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bacterial overgrowth** (e.g. group A streptococcus, *E. coli*) with significant erythema and pain: **consider cefalexin** per local antimicrobial guidelines.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval and vaginal conditions' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_and_vaginal_conditions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Sexual abuse occasionally presents as vulvovaginitis.** Discuss persistent, recurrent or multiple presentations with gynaecology.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval and vaginal conditions' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_and_vaginal_conditions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A normal variant** developing from 3 months and resolving spontaneously by 6 to 8 years; usually asymptomatic.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval and vaginal conditions' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_and_vaginal_conditions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If the child voids easily, no treatment.** Oestrogen cream or manual separation are **not recommended** (high recurrence; separation is painful). **Outflow obstruction:** consider a short course of oestrogen cream after discussion with gynaecology.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval and vaginal conditions' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_and_vaginal_conditions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Lichen sclerosus:** onset 5–7 years; itch, bleeding or discharge; pale atrophic patches. ⚠️ **Purpuric haemorrhage after scratching is occasionally mistaken for sexual abuse.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval and vaginal conditions' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_and_vaginal_conditions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Lichen sclerosus treatment:** reassurance, avoid irritants, treat constipation, barrier ointments short term; **a course of high- then medium-potency topical steroid is often required — seek specialist advice.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval and vaginal conditions' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_and_vaginal_conditions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Vulvodynia (pain 3 months or more without identifiable cause):** vulval care, pelvic floor physiotherapy, psychology if anxiety or depression, manage constipation; topical local anaesthetic short term only; **neuropathic agents (amitriptyline, gabapentin, pregabalin) only on specialist advice.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval and vaginal conditions' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_and_vaginal_conditions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Urethral prolapse:** chronic bleeding, pain, dysuria, straining; treat the precipitant (cough, constipation) and **refer to gynaecology** for topical oestrogen.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval and vaginal conditions' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_and_vaginal_conditions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult gynaecology** if the diagnosis is unclear, advice is needed, or a foreign body needs removal. ⚠️ **Suspected sexual assault: follow local guidelines; early specialist consultation is vital.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval and vaginal conditions' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_and_vaginal_conditions/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Transfer** if a vaginal foreign body is suspected and examination under anaesthetic is not available locally. **Discharge** once diagnosed with follow-up in place.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Vulval and vaginal conditions' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Vulval_and_vaginal_conditions/, retrieved 2026-09-23
